gaps.hint: past participle after 'have'; the verb takes no object
gaps.explanation: 'Rise' (rise, rose, risen) takes no object: sales have risen. 'Raise' takes an object: they raised prices.

gaps.sentence: The comedian was so ___ that everyone cried with laughter.
gaps.explanation: 'Funny' is an adjective describing something that makes you laugh; 'fun' describes enjoyable experiences.

gaps.sentence: The storm did considerable ___ to the harbour wall.
gaps.explanation: 'Do damage' — uncountable; 'damages' means money awarded in court.
'Especially' means in particular or above all; 'specially' means for one particular purpose.
'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.

gaps.sentence: Take my ___ and sell the car before the prices fall.
gaps.explanation: 'Take my advice' — the noun form follows the possessive.

gaps.sentence: Factory workers are paid ___ at the end of each week.
gaps.hint: pay for manual work, usually weekly
gaps.explanation: 'Wages' are paid weekly, often in cash, for manual or unskilled work; salaries are monthly.

gaps.sentence: The consultant will ___ us on every stage of the merger.
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the verb; 'advice' is the noun.
